trigger: The company determines it has had a computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to materially disrupt or degrade, covered services to a bank for four or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after that determination
notify: At least one bank-designated point of contact at each affected bank; if none was provided, the bank's CEO and CIO (or two people of comparable responsibility) by any reasonable means (53.4(a)(1)-(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 14 bank customers. Scheduled maintenance previously communicated is excluded (53.4(b))

obligation: Bank customers' own notice to their regulator (context)
citation: 12 CFR 53.3 (OCC) and the parallel FRB and FDIC rules
trigger: A bank determines that a notification incident has occurred
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank's determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank's duty. The company's notice and follow-up facts feed the bank's 36-hour clock

trigger: Confirmed security incident affecting the customer's services or data
deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation
notify: Each affected customer's designated security contact

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for a customer (unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected customer (the covered entity), with all information it needs to give its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a third-party agent when it maintains or processes personal information for customers (501.171(1)(h)). The customer then owes notices under 501.171(3)-(5)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company itself holds (employee records; customer contact and billing data) of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15-day extension possible with good cause given to the department)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the company's own personal information is involved

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (company's own data)
trigger: Breach of the company's own personal information affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (company's own data)
trigger: Company must notify more than 1,000 individuals at one time

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days); many states also require a service provider to notify the data owner (check each statute)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Customers' data subjects and the company's staff may live outside Florida; apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: FedRAMP incident communications (Class C Initial Incident Report)
citation: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: IEC-CSO-EFR; IEC-CSO-DPR; IEC-CSO-IIR
trigger: A FedRAMP Reportable Incident: an incident that affects, or is likely to affect, the confidentiality or integrity of federal customer data (PAIN-5 assumed unless estimated under IEC-CSO-EFI)
deadline: Class C: 1 hour for PAIN-3 to PAIN-5; 24 hours for PAIN-2; 1 business day for PAIN-1
notify: FedRAMP (fedramp_security@fedramp.gov); agency customers through each agency's own incident reporting procedure; all necessary parties through the trust center
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal customer or FedRAMP certification today. Applies from the first agency tenant (P03 readiness target)

obligation: FedRAMP ongoing and final incident reports
citation: FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026: IEC-CSO-OIR; IEC-CSO-FIR
trigger: A reported FedRAMP Reportable Incident is ongoing, then resolved with recovery complete
deadline: Class C ongoing updates: every 6 hours (PAIN-3 to PAIN-5), 24 hours (PAIN-2), 1 business day (PAIN-1). Final report: 6 hours (PAIN-3 to PAIN-5) or 1 business day (PAIN-1 and PAIN-2) after resolution
notify: Same parties as the initial report

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck coverage of IT sector providers when final

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information or a covered contractor information system
notify: DoD (DIBNet portal); subcontractors also notify the prime
applies_at_this_tier: No - no DoD contracts and the MSA prohibits covered defense information

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts today

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment (for example if the malicious script encrypted customer servers)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI (IC3 or field office); CISA reporting
trigger: Compromise of a tool that reaches many customers
deadline: As early as practical; supports OFAC mitigation and shared threat intelligence
Per policy; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors

obligation: RMM vendor incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: RMM vendor terms (no notice clause today; POAM-020 adds one)
trigger: The RMM vendor detects a compromise of its platform or of the company's tenant
deadline: None in the current contract (gap); target 72 hours or less
